Of course, the old hands on the ward were helping to shield her from the worst of it. Rachel, the veteran nurse, had been warning her about the 8 patients she was assigned to care for tonight. "Trust me, honey," Rachel said, "Ezekiel's gonna be a handful, he's off his meds. Jamal's gonna try to sneak out of his restraints, and Sarah's gonna get nasty with the new kid." 

But the one who really made her nervous was Alex. "Keep a close eye on Alex," Rachel said, "he's our 'lucky' one, always hovering on the edge. We've had to intervene multiple times, and he's always so grateful afterwards, but I'm scared of him. There's something...off about him." 

Karen tried to brush off Rachel's concerns, but as the night wore on, she couldn't shake the feeling of unease. Alex was indeed quiet, and subdued, and seemed almost eerily grateful to be alive, like he was re-living every moment.

As the night wore on, a call went out to Code Brown. One of the patients had tried to take their own life. Karen rushed to the scene, her heart pounding. She got to the scene, and saw Alex, hanging from the noose, his eyes open and staring at her.
